topic: Automating scientific peer review with LLMs
graph_title: Does Claim-Level Grounding Actually Close the Attack Surface in LLM Peer Review? A Cross-Paradigm Adversarial Audit
web_title: Claim-Conditioned Multimodal Review: Teaching LLM Peer Reviewers to Audit Figures Against Text, Not Just Pixels
graph_novelty_reason: Adversarial/perturbation attacks on holistic LLM reviewers are well covered in 2024-25 work, so the contribution reduces to porting that battery to the claim-verification paradigm, which is a plausible but incremental cross-paradigm extension — the two architecture-specific attacks (citation poisoning of the grounding step, execution gaming) are the genuinely fresh element.
graph_feasibility_reason: The attack battery, control condition, and flip-rate outcome stratified by executable vs non-executable claims are concrete and runnable, but the study depends on faithfully reimplementing "FactReview" (a citation I cannot verify and which may be misattributed or nascent) and on reconciling two non-commensurable outcome metrics — score shift vs evidence-label distribution shift — which weakens cross-paradigm comparison.
web_novelty_reason: Bridging text-only LLM review agents with biomedical figure-integrity forensics via claim-conditioned cross-modal consistency checking (panel labels vs stated conditions, visible lanes/points vs reported n) is a genuinely new framing and measurement, though MLLM-based image-integrity screening is beginning to appear, capping this below the top band.
web_feasibility_reason: The Retraction Watch/PubPeer positives plus matched clean controls and the blind actionability rating give a clear measurable design, but execution faces serious practical gaps: obtaining licensed access to Imagetwin/Proofig as baselines, PDF figure/panel extraction at scale, very noisy and small positive labels (PubPeer allegations ≠ confirmed manipulation), and known MLLM weakness at fine-grained panel matching.
same_idea_reason: Both concern trustworthiness of LLM peer review and both invoke "claim-level" reasoning, but A is a text-only adversarial robustness audit comparing two review architectures while B builds a multimodal figure-integrity reviewer and benchmarks it against image-forensics tools — different gaps, data, and measurements.

topic: Automating scientific peer review with LLMs
graph_title: Does Claim-Level Grounding Actually Close the Attack Surface in LLM Peer Review? A Cross-Paradigm Adversarial Audit
web_title: Claim-Conditioned Multimodal Review: Teaching LLM Peer Reviewers to Audit Figures Against Text, Not Just Pixels
graph_novelty_reason: Attack batteries against LLM reviewers (prompt injection, prestige bias, perturbation analyses) are already well published, so the contribution is mainly porting them to a newer claim-verification architecture, with the two architecture-specific attacks — retrieval/related-work poisoning and execution gaming — being the actually novel pieces.
graph_feasibility_reason: Seven attacks plus control with flip-rate as a primary outcome stratified by executable vs. non-executable claims is a clean, decisive design, but it hinges on faithfully reimplementing "FactReview," a citation I cannot verify and which may be fabricated or misattributed, and comparing an accept-score shift against an "evidence-label distribution shift" across paradigms is a metric-commensurability gap left unresolved.
web_novelty_reason: Bridging text-only LLM review agents with biomedical figure-integrity forensics via *claim-conditioned* cross-modal auditing (does the panel match what the caption/methods assert, not just pixel duplication) is a genuinely new framing, though multimodal figure-checking and VLM duplication-detection probes have begun to appear.
web_feasibility_reason: The design is concrete with named comparators (forensic tool, original editorial outcome), a blind actionability rating, and a case/control corpus, but the benchmark has real hazards the proposal glosses: PubPeer/Retraction Watch labels are paper-level and post-hoc contaminated, "clean" controls are only presumed clean, panel-pair comparison scales combinatorially, and severe class imbalance makes specificity estimates fragile.
same_idea_reason: Both target LLM peer review, but A builds a multimodal figure–text integrity auditor evaluated on misconduct detection, while B runs an adversarial robustness audit comparing holistic vs. claim-verification review architectures — different gaps, methods, and outcomes.

topic: Fully autonomous end-to-end AI scientists for machine-learning research
graph_title: Does Self-Evolution in Autonomous AI Scientists Optimize for Looking Rigorous Rather Than Being Rigorous? Auditing Goodhart Drift in Iterative AI-Scientist Pipelines
web_title: Portfolio-Level Sequential Testing with False-Discovery Control for Autonomous AI Scientists
graph_novelty_reason: Longitudinal, causal test of whether a self-evolving AI-scientist's own review score Goodharts into "looking rigorous" — reward-hacking of LLM judges and cross-sectional pitfall audits are known, but the generational drift measurement plus audit-as-fitness swap is a genuinely new framing.
graph_feasibility_reason: Concrete and executable with synthetic tasks where legitimate vs. illegitimate choices are ground-truthed and a clear two-curve divergence measurement, though the independent rubric judge is itself an LLM sharing the failure modes it audits (no stated human calibration of it), many-generation evolution over real ML tasks is expensive, and several cited anchors (EvoScientist, BiomniBench/FlowBench) are obscure enough that misattribution is a risk.
web_novelty_reason: Importing online FDR control (LORD/SAFFRON, alpha-investing) as the promotion currency in a successive-halving portfolio of agent-generated hypotheses is a real cross-literature transplant not, to my knowledge, done in AI-scientist pipelines, though each component is individually standard.
web_feasibility_reason: The scheduler, robustness probe, and matched-compute baselines are well specified and buildable, but the statistical core is shaky — seed/split reruns give a perturbation-stability p-value, not a valid null for "this is a true discovery," so the nominal FDR target is not calibrated to the replication ground truth used for evaluation, and the independent-replication arbiter plus N parallel full experiments is a heavy lift.
same_idea_reason: Both attack the unreliability of self-judged AI-scientist outputs, but A is a diagnostic/auditing study of Goodhart drift in self-evolution loops while B is a systems intervention replacing the promotion statistic with FDR-controlled portfolio scheduling.

topic: Fully autonomous end-to-end AI scientists for machine-learning research
graph_title: Does Self-Evolution in Autonomous AI Scientists Optimize for Looking Rigorous Rather Than Being Rigorous? Auditing Goodhart Drift in Iterative AI-Scientist Pipelines
web_title: Portfolio-Level Sequential Testing with False-Discovery Control for Autonomous AI Scientists
graph_novelty_reason: A longitudinal, causal test of Goodhart drift between an AI-scientist's own self-review fitness and an independent process-level audit is a sensible new measurement, but reward hacking of LLM self-evaluation in self-improvement loops is a heavily explored theme, so this reads as a well-targeted extension rather than a new idea.
graph_feasibility_reason: Synthetic tasks with known-illegitimate choices (touchable test split, metric/benchmark menus) give controllable ground truth and the two-trajectory divergence plus audit-guided-fitness arm is a clear, decisive measurement; main risks are that the auditing judge is itself an LLM sharing the failure modes it grades, the expert evaluation is unspecified, and multi-generation evolution runs are costly.
web_novelty_reason: Casting an autonomous scientist's hypothesis stream as an online-FDR-controlled portfolio, with robustness-under-perturbation (not judge score) as the promotion statistic, is a genuinely new mechanism-level framing even though its two ingredients (successive halving, LORD/SAFFRON) are standard elsewhere.
web_feasibility_reason: The design is concrete with named baselines and a replication-based ground truth, but the statistical core is under-specified — turning seed/split reruns into valid p-values or e-values against a stated null is nontrivial, meaningful FDR estimation needs many arms, and end-to-end independent replication of every promoted finding is very compute- and labor-expensive.
same_idea_reason: Both attack the verification/self-deception gap in autonomous scientists, but A proposes a statistical compute-allocation mechanism (FDR-gated portfolio scheduling measured by replication rate) while B proposes a diagnostic audit of whether iterative self-evolution causally amplifies methodological pitfalls.

graph_title: Error-Targeted Literature Retrieval for Hybrid Hypothesis Generation
web_title: Calibrated Hypothesis Generation: Conformal Confidence for LLM-Proposed Scientific Hypotheses
graph_novelty_reason: Closing the loop so that the wrong-example bank steers literature retrieval is a sensible and not-obviously-published twist on HypoRefine, but it is essentially boosting-style residual-driven adaptive retrieval (a well-known pattern from FLARE/self-RAG-type work) transplanted into an existing pipeline, so incremental rather than strikingly new.
graph_feasibility_reason: Everything is concrete and buildable on public code — named baselines, a matched-retrieval-budget untargeted ablation that cleanly isolates "targeting" from "more retrieval", and HypoBench's synthetic ground-truth recovery rate as a decisive quantitative outcome; the main soft spot is that clustering the wrong-example bank and turning clusters into good queries may itself be brittle.
web_novelty_reason: Measuring probabilistic calibration of hypothesis-generator confidence against real future-publication validation, and converting it into conformal selection sets, is a genuinely fresh framing for this subfield even though calibration and conformal methods for LLMs are themselves mature.
web_feasibility_reason: Executable in principle but the measurement rests on a noisy, low-base-rate, LLM-judged "matched a future paper" label as ground truth for calibration, exchangeability is clearly violated across time and domains (undermining the conformal guarantee), the coverage statement as phrased is non-standard for split conformal, and part of the cited grounding (HindSight, "Continuous Knowledge Metabolism") is obscure enough that the reported novelty/validation anti-correlation cannot be taken on faith.
same_idea_reason: A improves generation by making retrieval reactive to explanatory failures; B leaves generation alone and instead measures/calibrates confidence in generated hypotheses against future literature — different gaps and entirely different studies.

graph_title: Error-Targeted Literature Retrieval for Hybrid Hypothesis Generation
web_title: Calibrated Hypothesis Generation: Conformal Confidence for LLM-Proposed Scientific Hypotheses
graph_novelty_reason: Closing the loop so that the wrong-example bank steers literature retrieval is a genuinely unexploited seam between HypoGeniC/HypoRefine and active/adaptive RAG (FLARE-style), but it is a fairly natural "make retrieval error-conditioned" combination of two existing mechanisms rather than a new mechanism or measurement.
graph_feasibility_reason: Built on real, open codebases and an existing controlled-difficulty benchmark with a named quantitative baseline (38.8% recovery), a clearly falsifiable difficulty-dependent prediction, and — crucially — the matched-retrieval-budget untargeted ablation that isolates targeting from retrieval volume; main risks are retrieval-corpus specification and variance across seeds, not conceptual gaps.
web_novelty_reason: Porting calibration/conformal machinery to hypothesis generation with temporal-holdout ground truth is a sensible and not-obviously-published extension, but both components (verbalized-confidence calibration, conformal/FDR-controlled candidate selection à la conformal selection for drug discovery) are well-established elsewhere, so the contribution is mostly a new application domain plus the cross-domain-vs-incremental miscalibration sub-analysis.
web_feasibility_reason: Calibration measurement is straightforward, but the ground-truth label ("was this hypothesis validated by a post-cutoff paper?") is the crux and is left to noisy LLM/paper matching over thousands of items, the conformal framing is conceptually muddled (coverage of *what* random variable, and exchangeability is plainly violated when calibrating on past hypotheses to deploy on future ones), and at least two of the anchor citations (HindSight, "Continuous Knowledge Metabolism") plus the specific novelty/validation anti-correlation claim look uncertain or possibly misattributed.
same_idea_reason: A is an evaluation/uncertainty-quantification study measuring and conformalizing confidence in generated hypotheses, while B is a method paper adding error-conditioned literature retrieval to a hybrid generation pipeline — different gaps, different pipelines, different measurements.
